sentences.zh: 秦國大長公主，太祖同母妹也。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Qin was a younger sister of the same mother as Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of the State of Qin was Emperor Taizu's younger uterine sister.

sentences.zh: 初適米福德，福德卒。

translations.literal: At first she married Mi Fude; Fude died.
translations.idiomatic: She was first married to Mi Fude, who died.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，，封燕國長公主，再適忠武軍節度使高懷德，賜第興寧坊。

translations.literal: When Taizu acceded, she was enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Yan, then married again to Gao Huaide, military commissioner of the Zhongwu army, and was granted a residence in Xingning Ward.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, she was made Princess of Yan, then remarried to Gao Huaide, military commissioner of the Zhongwu army, and given a mansion in Xingning Ward.

sentences.zh: 十月薨，太祖臨哭，廢朝五日，賜諡恭懿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month she died; Taizu came in person to mourn, court was suspended for five days, and she was granted the posthumous name Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the tenth month. Taizu mourned at her residence in person, suspended court for five days, and gave her the posthumous epithet Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 真宗追封大長公主。，

translations.literal: Zhenzong posthumously enfeoffed her as Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong posthumously raised her to Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 改秦國。，

translations.literal: Her title was changed to the State of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Her fief was redesignated as the State of Qin.

sentences.zh: 改封恭懿大長帝姬。

translations.literal: She was further changed to Grand Imperial Princess Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: She was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 有姊一人，未笄而夭。

translations.literal: She had one elder sister, who died before coming of age.
translations.idiomatic: She had one older sister, who died before she reached marriageable age.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，追封陳國長公主。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In 962, she was posthumously made Princess of the State of Chen.

sentences.zh: 元符改封荊國大長公主。

translations.literal: Under Yuanfu, her title was changed to Grand Princess of the State of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era, she was redesignated Grand Princess of the State of Jing.

sentences.zh: 政和改封恭獻大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Gongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huizong's Zhenghe reign, she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Gongxian.

sentences.zh: 太祖六女

translations.literal: Six Daughters of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: The Six Daughters of Emperor Taizu

sentences.zh: 太祖六女。

translations.literal: Six Daughters of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: The Six Daughters of Emperor Taizu

sentences.zh: 申國、成國、永國三公主，皆早亡。

translations.literal: The Princesses of Shen, Cheng, and Yong all died young.
translations.idiomatic: The princesses of Shen, Cheng, and Yong all died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 魏國大長公主，，封昭慶公主，下嫁左衛將軍王承衍，賜第景龍門外。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Wei was enfeoffed as Princess Zhaoqing, married down to Wang Chengyan, General of the Left Guard, and granted a residence outside Jinglong Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Wei was made Princess Zhaoqing, married Wang Chengyan, a general of the Left Guard, and given a mansion outside Jinglong Gate.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，進封鄭國。，

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, she was promoted to Princess of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 改封秦國。

translations.literal: Her title was changed to Princess of the State of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Her fief was redesignated as the State of Qin.

sentences.zh: 真宗，進長公主。

translations.literal: Under Zhenzong, she was advanced to Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhenzong she was raised to Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 薨，賜諡賢肅。

translations.literal: She died and was granted the posthumous name Xiansu.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she received the posthumous epithet Xiansu.

sentences.zh: 元符改封魏國大長公主。

translations.literal: Under Yuanfu, her title was changed to Grand Princess of the State of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era she was redesignated Grand Princess of Wei.

sentences.zh: 政和改賢肅大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Xiansu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Xiansu.

sentences.zh: 魯國大長公主，，封延慶公主，下嫁左衛將軍石保吉。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Lu was enfeoffed as Princess Yanqing and married down to Shi Baoji, General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Lu was made Princess Yanqing and married Shi Baoji, a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，進封許國。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, she was promoted to Princess of Xu.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，改晉國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, her title was changed to the State of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In 990 her fief was redesignated as the State of Jin.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，進長公主。，

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong, she was advanced to Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhenzong's reign she was raised to Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 進大長公主。

translations.literal: She was further advanced to Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: Her rank was further raised to Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 薨，賜諡賢靖。

translations.literal: She died and was granted the posthumous name Xianjing.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she received the posthumous epithet Xianjing.

sentences.zh: 元符改封魯國。

translations.literal: Under Yuanfu, her title was changed to the State of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era she was redesignated Princess of Lu.

sentences.zh: 政和改賢靖大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Xianjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Xianjing.

sentences.zh: 陳國大長公主，開寶五年，封永慶公主，下嫁右衛將軍魏咸信。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Chen, in the fifth year of Kaibao, was enfeoffed as Princess Yongqing and married down to Wei Xianxin, General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Chen, in 972, was made Princess Yongqing and married Wei Xianxin, a general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，進封虢國。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, she was promoted to Princess of Guo.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，改齊國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, her title was changed to the State of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In 990 her fief was redesignated as the State of Qi.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，進許國長公主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhenzong's reign she was raised to Princess of Xu.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡貞惠，後改恭惠。，

translations.literal: She died; her posthumous name was Zhenhui, later changed to Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: She died and was given the epithet Zhenhui, later changed to Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 追封大長公主。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 元符改封陳國。

translations.literal: Under Yuanfu, her title was changed to the State of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era she was redesignated Princess of Chen.

sentences.zh: 政和改賢惠大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Xianhui.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Xianhui.

sentences.zh: 太宗七女

translations.literal: Seven Daughters of Taizong
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Daughters of Emperor Taizong

sentences.zh: 太宗七女。

translations.literal: Seven Daughters of Taizong
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Daughters of Emperor Taizong

sentences.zh: 長滕國公主，早亡。

translations.literal: The elder Princess of the State of Teng died young.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Princess of Teng, also died young.

sentences.zh: 徐國大長公主，，封蔡國，下嫁左衛將軍吳元扆。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Xu was enfeoffed as Princess of Cai and married down to Wu Yuanyi, General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Xu was made Princess of Cai and married Wu Yuanyi, a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，改魏國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, her title was changed to the State of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In 990 her fief was redesignated as the State of Wei.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡英惠。，

translations.literal: She died and was granted the posthumous name Yinghui.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she received the posthumous epithet Yinghui.

sentences.zh: 追封燕國長公主。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made Princess of Yan.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年，進大長公主。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou, she was advanced to Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: In 1036 her rank was raised to Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 元符改徐國。

translations.literal: Under Yuanfu, her title was changed to the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era her fief was redesignated as the State of Xu.

sentences.zh: 政和改英惠大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Yinghui.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Yinghui.

sentences.zh: 邠國大長公主，太平興國七年為尼，號員明大師。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Bin, in the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo became a nun, with the style name Master Yuanming.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Bin took Buddhist orders in 982, the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, and adopted the religious name Master Yuanming.

sentences.zh: 八年卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died the following year.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，追封曹國長公主。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: In 997 she was posthumously made Princess of the State of Cao.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年，進大長公主。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou, she was advanced to Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: In 1036 her rank was raised to Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 元符改邠國。

translations.literal: Under Yuanfu, her title was changed to the State of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era her fief was redesignated as the State of Bin.

sentences.zh: 揚國大長公主，至道三年，封宣慈長公主。，

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Yang, in the third year of Zhidao, was enfeoffed as Princess Xuanci.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Yang, in 997, was made Princess Xuanci.

sentences.zh: 進魯國，下嫁左衛將軍柴宗慶，賜第普寧坊。

translations.literal: She was advanced to Princess of the State of Lu, married down to Chai Zongqing, General of the Left Guard, and granted a residence in Puning Ward.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to Princess of Lu, married Chai Zongqing, a general of the Left Guard, and given a mansion in Puning Ward.

sentences.zh: 宗慶，禹錫之孫，帝命主以婦禮謁禹錫第。

translations.literal: Zongqing was a grandson of Yu Xi; the Emperor ordered the Princess to pay a visit to Yu Xi's residence using the rites due a daughter-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqing was a grandson of Yu Xi; the emperor directed the princess to call on Yu Xi's household observing daughter-in-law propriety.

sentences.zh: 曆徙韓、魏、徐、福四國。

translations.literal: She was transferred in succession through the four states of Han, Wei, Xu, and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Her fief was successively redesignated as Han, Wei, Xu, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，進鄧國大長公主。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended, she was advanced to Grand Princess of the State of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, she was raised to Grand Princess of Deng.

sentences.zh: 薨，追封晉國，諡愍靖。

translations.literal: She died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Jin, with the posthumous name Minjing.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she was posthumously made Princess of Jin, with the posthumous epithet Minjing.

sentences.zh: 元符封揚國。

translations.literal: Under Yuanfu, she was enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era she was made Princess of Yang.

sentences.zh: 政和改和靖大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Hejing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Hejing.

sentences.zh: 主性妒，宗慶無子，以兄子為後。

translations.literal: The Princess was jealous by nature; Zongqing had no sons, so they took his elder brother's son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was jealous by nature. Zongqing had no sons, so they adopted his elder brother's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 雍國大長公主，至道三年，封賢懿長公主。，

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Yong, in the third year of Zhidao, was enfeoffed as Princess Xianyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Yong, in 997, was made Princess Xianyi.

sentences.zh: 下嫁右衛將軍王貽永，進封鄭國，賜第。

translations.literal: She married down to Wang Yiyong, General of the Right Guard, was advanced to Princess of the State of Zheng, and was granted a residence.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wang Yiyong, a general of the Right Guard, was promoted to Princess of Zheng, and received a mansion.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡懿順。

translations.literal: She died and was granted the posthumous name Yishun.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she received the posthumous epithet Yishun.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年，追封大長公主。，

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: In 1036 she was posthumously made Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 改韓國。

translations.literal: Her title was changed to the State of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Her fief was redesignated as the State of Han.

sentences.zh: 徽宗改封雍國。

translations.literal: Huizong changed her title to Princess of the State of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong redesignated her Grand Princess of Yong.

sentences.zh: 政和改懿順大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Yishun.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Yishun.

sentences.zh: 衛國大長公主，至道三年，封壽昌長公主。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Wei, in the third year of Zhidao, was enfeoffed as Princess Shouchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Wei, in 997, was made Princess Shouchang.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，進封陳國，改吳國，號報慈正覺大師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Chen, changed to the State of Wu, and given the style name Master Baoci Zhengjue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1009 she was promoted to Princess of Chen, redesignated Princess of Wu, and given the religious name Master Baoci Zhengjue.

sentences.zh: 改楚國，又改邠國。，

translations.literal: Her title was changed to the State of Chu, then again to the State of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Her fief was redesignated as Chu, then as Bin.

sentences.zh: 改建國。，

translations.literal: Her title was changed to the State of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Her fief was redesignated as the State of Jian.

sentences.zh: 封申國大長公主。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: She was made Grand Princess of Shen.

sentences.zh: 薨，賜諡慈明。

translations.literal: She died and was granted the posthumous name Ciming.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she received the posthumous epithet Ciming.

sentences.zh: 徽宗改衛國。

translations.literal: Huizong changed her title to the State of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong redesignated her Princess of Wei.

sentences.zh: 政和改慈明大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Ciming.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Ciming.

sentences.zh: 荊國大長公主，幼不好弄，未嘗出房闥。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Jing from childhood did not care for play and never left the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Jing disliked childish amusements from youth and never left the women's apartments.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗發寶藏，令諸女擇取之，欲以觀其志，主獨無所取。

translations.literal: Taizong once opened the treasure stores and had his daughters choose from them, wishing to observe their inclinations; the Princess alone took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once opened the imperial treasure vaults and let his daughters choose what they wished, to test their character; the princess alone took nothing.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，封萬壽長公主，改隨國，下嫁駙馬都尉李遵勖。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, she was enfeoffed as Princess Wanshou, then Princess of Sui, and married down to Li Zunxu, Commissioner-in-Ordinary Attached to the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, she was made Princess Wanshou, then Princess of Sui, and married Li Zunxu, imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 舊制選尚者降其父為兄弟行，時遵勖父繼昌亡恙，主因繼昌生日以舅禮謁之。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when a consort was chosen the father of the groom was lowered to the rank of a brother; at the time Zunxu's father Jichang was still alive and well, so on Jichang's birthday the Princess paid him a visit with the rites due a maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom a chosen consort's father-in-law was treated as a brother in rank; since Li Zunxu's father Jichang was still alive, the princess visited him on his birthday with the courtesy due a maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，密以兼衣、寶帶、器模式幣助其為壽。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he secretly sent layered garments, jeweled belts, vessels, silks, and cash to help with the birthday celebration.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of this, the emperor secretly sent layered robes, jeweled belts, vessels, silks, and cash to help honor the occasion.

sentences.zh: 遵勖賓客皆一時賢士，每燕集，主必親視饔饎。

translations.literal: Zunxu's guests were all worthy men of the time; at every banquet the Princess personally oversaw the cooking.
translations.idiomatic: Zunxu's guests were all men of talent; at every feast the princess personally supervised the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 嘗有盜入主第，帝命有司訊捕。

translations.literal: Once a thief entered the Princess's residence; the Emperor ordered the authorities to investigate and arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Once a thief broke into her mansion; the emperor ordered officials to investigate and apprehend him.

sentences.zh: 主請出所逮系人，以私錢募告者，果得真盜，法當死，復請貰之。

translations.literal: The Princess requested the release of those detained, used her private funds to offer a reward for information, and thereby obtained the real thief; by law he deserved death, yet she again requested that he be ransomed.
translations.idiomatic: She asked that the detainees be released, posted a private reward for information, and thereby caught the real thief; though he deserved death by law, she again petitioned to redeem his life.

sentences.zh: 曆封越、宿、鄂、冀四國。，

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed in succession through the four states of Yue, Su, E, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Her fiefs were successively Yue, Su, E, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 進魏國。

translations.literal: She was advanced to Princess of the State of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to Princess of Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，遵勖出守許州，暴得疾，主亟欲馳視之，左右白：須奏得報乃可行，主不待報而往，從者裁五六人。

translations.literal: At first, when Zunxu went out to govern Xuzhou and suddenly fell ill, the Princess urgently wished to hurry to see him; attendants reported that one must memorialize and receive a reply before going; the Princess did not wait for the reply and went, with only five or six followers.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Li Zunxu was posted to Xuzhou and fell suddenly ill, the princess was desperate to rush to his side. Her attendants said she must petition the throne and await approval before leaving; she set out without waiting, accompanied by only five or six people.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，遽命內侍督諸縣邏兵以衛主車。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he immediately ordered palace eunuchs to supervise patrol troops of the various counties to guard the Princess's carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of this, the emperor at once dispatched palace eunuchs to mobilize county patrol forces along her route to escort her carriage.

sentences.zh: 其後居夫喪，衰麻未嘗去身，服除，不復禦華麗。

translations.literal: Afterward, during her husband's mourning, she never removed her coarse hemp garments; when the mourning period ended, she no longer wore ornate dress.
translations.idiomatic: After his death she observed mourning so strictly that she never put off her hemp garments; when the mourning period ended, she refused ever to dress in finery again.

sentences.zh: 嘗燕禁中，帝親為簪花，辭曰：「自誓不復為此久矣。」

translations.literal: Once at a banquet in the Forbidden precinct, the Emperor personally placed flowers in her hair; she declined, saying, "I vowed long ago never to do this again."
translations.idiomatic: At a palace banquet the emperor himself tried to pin flowers in her hair; she refused, saying, "I swore long ago that I would never do this again."

sentences.zh: 嘗因浴僕地，傷右肱，帝遣內侍責侍者，主曰：「早衰力弱，不任步趨，非左右之過。」

translations.literal: Once when she slipped while bathing in the servants' quarters and injured her right arm, the Emperor sent a palace eunuch to rebuke the attendants; the Princess said, "I am early failing in strength and cannot manage walking—this is not the fault of those beside me."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion she slipped while bathing a servant's quarters and hurt her right arm. The emperor sent a eunuch to punish her attendants, but she said, "My strength has failed early; I can scarcely walk—this is no fault of those around me."

sentences.zh: 由是悉得免。

translations.literal: Thus they were all exempted from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They were all spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 主善筆劄，喜圖史，能為歌詩，尤善女工之事。

translations.literal: The Princess was skilled at letters, fond of histories and chronicles, could compose songs and poems, and was especially adept at women's crafts.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished at correspondence, loved histories and annals, wrote verse, and excelled at needlework and other domestic arts.

sentences.zh: 嘗誡諸子以「忠義自守，無恃吾以速悔尤」，視他子與己出均。

translations.literal: She once admonished her sons: "Hold to loyalty and righteousness; do not rely on me to hasten remorse and blame," and treated other people's sons the same as her own.
translations.idiomatic: She once warned her sons, "Keep to loyalty and righteousness; do not count on my favor to escape the consequences of your faults," and treated her stepsons no differently from her own children.

sentences.zh: 及病目，帝挾醫診視，自后妃以下皆至第候問。

translations.literal: When she grew ill in the eyes, the Emperor himself brought physicians to examine her; from the empress and consorts downward, all came to her residence to inquire after her.
translations.idiomatic: When her eyes failed, the emperor himself escorted physicians to her mansion; from the empress and consorts down, the entire inner court came to inquire after her health.

sentences.zh: 帝親舐其目，左右皆感泣，帝亦悲慟曰：「先帝伯仲之籍十有四人，今獨存大主，奈何嬰斯疾！」

translations.literal: The Emperor personally licked her eyes; all around were moved to tears; the Emperor also grieved and said, "Among the fourteen in the register of the late Emperor's brothers and sisters, only the Grand Princess remains—how can she suffer this illness!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor licked her afflicted eyes himself; everyone present wept, and he lamented, "Of the fourteen brothers and sisters recorded in my father's line, only the Grand Princess survives—how can she be stricken with this disease!"

sentences.zh: 復顧問子孫所欲，主曰：「豈可以母病邀賞邪？」

translations.literal: He again asked what her sons and grandsons desired; the Princess said, "How can one use a mother's illness to seek rewards?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked what favors her sons and grandsons might want; she replied, "How could one use a mother's illness to seek rewards?"

sentences.zh: 齎白金三千兩，辭不受。

translations.literal: They presented three thousand taels of white silver; she declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: They offered three thousand taels of silver, but she refused to accept them.

sentences.zh: 帝因謂從臣曰：「大主之疾，倘可移於朕，亦所不避也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor then said to his attendants, "If the Grand Princess's illness could be transferred to Us, We would not shrink from it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told his attendants, "If the Grand Princess's illness could be shifted onto me, I would not hesitate to take it."

sentences.zh: 主雖喪明，平居隱幾，沖淡自若。

translations.literal: Though the Princess had lost her sight, in daily life she reclined at her couch, calm and self-possessed.
translations.idiomatic: Though blind, in daily life she sat quietly at her couch, serene and untroubled.

sentences.zh: 誡諸子曰：「汝父遺令：柩中無藏金玉，時衣數襲而已。

translations.literal: She admonished her sons: "Your father's testament: in the coffin place no gold or jade—only a few sets of ordinary garments.
translations.idiomatic: She warned her sons, "Your father left instructions: let the coffin hold no gold or jade—only a few sets of everyday clothes.

sentences.zh: 吾歿後當亦如是。」

translations.literal: After my death you should do the same."
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, do the same for me."

sentences.zh: 皇祐三年薨，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangyou she died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1051 at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 帝臨奠，輟視朝五日。

translations.literal: The Emperor came in person to mourn, and court audiences were suspended for five days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned at her residence in person and suspended court for five days.

sentences.zh: 追封齊國大長公主，諡獻穆。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Qi, with the posthumous name Xianmu.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made Grand Princess of Qi with the epithet Xianmu.

sentences.zh: 徽宗改封荊國。

translations.literal: Huizong changed her title to Princess of the State of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong redesignated her Princess of Jing.

sentences.zh: 政和改獻穆大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Xianmu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Xianmu.

sentences.zh: 真宗二女

translations.literal: Two Daughters of Zhenzong
translations.idiomatic: The Two Daughters of Emperor Zhenzong

sentences.zh: 真宗二女。

translations.literal: Two Daughters of Zhenzong
translations.idiomatic: The Two Daughters of Emperor Zhenzong

sentences.zh: 長惠國公主，早亡。

translations.literal: The elder Princess of the State of Hui died young.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Princess of Hui, died young.

sentences.zh: 升國大長公主，初入道。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Sheng first entered the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Sheng first took Buddhist orders.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，封衛國長公主，號清虛靈照大師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao, she was enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Wei, with the style name Master Qingxu Lingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1033 she was made Princess of Wei and given the religious name Master Qingxu Lingzhao.

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年，追封魯國，諡昭懷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qingli, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Lu, with the posthumous name Zhaohuai.
translations.idiomatic: In 1047 she was posthumously made Princess of Lu, with the posthumous epithet Zhaohuai.

sentences.zh: 徽宗改封升國大長公主。

translations.literal: Under Huizong, her title was changed to Grand Princess of the State of Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong redesignated her Grand Princess of Sheng.

sentences.zh: 政和改昭大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Zhao.

sentences.zh: 仁宗十三女

translations.literal: Thirteen Daughters of Renzong
translations.idiomatic: The Thirteen Daughters of Emperor Renzong

sentences.zh: 仁宗十三女。

translations.literal: Thirteen Daughters of Renzong
translations.idiomatic: The Thirteen Daughters of Emperor Renzong

sentences.zh: 徐國、鄧國、鎮國、楚國、商國、魯國、唐國、陳國、豫國九公主，皆早亡。

translations.literal: The Princesses of Xu, Deng, Zhen, Chu, Shang, Lu, Tang, Chen, and Yu—all nine—died young.
translations.idiomatic: The princesses of Xu, Deng, Zhen, Chu, Shang, Lu, Tang, Chen, and Yu—all nine—died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 周、陳國大長公主，帝長女也。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of Zhou and Chen—she was the Emperor's eldest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Zhou and Chen was the emperor's eldest daughter.

sentences.zh: 寶元二年，封福康。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoyuan, she was enfeoffed as Fukang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1039 she received the title Fukang.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，進封袞國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1057 she was promoted to Princess of the State of Yan.

sentences.zh: 主幼警慧，性純孝。

translations.literal: The Princess from childhood was quick-witted, and by nature utterly filial.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was exceptionally bright and devoted in her filial piety.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗不豫，主侍左右，徒跣籲天，乞以身代。

translations.literal: When the Emperor once fell ill, the Princess attended at his side, went barefoot and cried to Heaven, begging to substitute her body for his.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, she kept constant vigil at his side, went barefoot, and prayed to Heaven to accept her life in place of his.

sentences.zh: 帝隆愛之。

translations.literal: The Emperor cherished her deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doted on her.

sentences.zh: 帝念章懿太后不及享天下養，故擇其兄子李瑋使尚主。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful that Empress Dowager Zhangyi had not lived to enjoy the world's nurture, therefore chose her elder brother's son Li Wei to marry the Princess.
translations.idiomatic: Because Empress Dowager Zhangyi had died before enjoying the honors of the throne, the emperor chose her nephew Li Wei as the princess's consort.

sentences.zh: 瑋樸陋，與主積不相能。

translations.literal: Wei was plain and uncouth; he and the Princess over time could not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was coarse and unrefined, and the couple grew increasingly incompatible.

sentences.zh: 主中夜扣皇城門入訴，瑋皇懼自劾。

translations.literal: At midnight the Princess knocked on the Imperial City gate to enter and complain; Wei in fear memorialized against himself.
translations.idiomatic: She knocked on the imperial city gate in the middle of the night to plead her case at court; Li Wei, terrified, submitted a confession of his own faults.

sentences.zh: 諫官王陶論宮門夜開，乞繩治護衛，御史又共論主第內臣多不謹，帝為黜都監梁懷一輩十餘人。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Wang Tao discussed the palace gate opening at night and requested that the guards be bound and punished; censors together also discussed how many inner eunuchs at the Princess's residence were not careful; the Emperor thereupon dismissed more than ten persons including the chief superintendent Liang Huaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Wang Tao protested the opening of the palace gate at night and called for the guards to be punished; censors jointly criticized the lax conduct of eunuchs in the princess's household, and the emperor dismissed more than a dozen of them, including chief superintendent Liang Huaiyi.

sentences.zh: 後數年不復協，詔出瑋於外，主降封沂，屏居內廷。

translations.literal: After several years they were again not in harmony; an edict sent Wei outside, the Princess was demoted to Princess of Yi, and confined to the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: After several more years of discord, an edict banished Li Wei from court, demoted her to Princess of Yi, and confined her within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，復召瑋，使為附馬都尉如初。

translations.literal: After a long time, Wei was again summoned and made Commissioner-in-Ordinary Attached to the Palace as before.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval Li Wei was recalled and restored to his post as imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，進越國長公主。

translations.literal: When Yingzong ascended, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, she was promoted to Princess of Yue.

sentences.zh: 神宗治平四年，進楚國大長公主。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping under Shenzong, she was advanced to Grand Princess of the State of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1067, under Emperor Shenzong, she was raised to Grand Princess of Chu.

sentences.zh: 薨，年三十三。

translations.literal: She died at thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 以瑋奉主無狀，貶陳州。

translations.literal: Because Wei's conduct toward the Princess was unseemly, he was demoted to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Wei's conduct toward the princess was unseemly, he was banished to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 輔臣議諡，帝以主事仁祖孝，命曰莊孝，追封秦國。

translations.literal: The chief ministers deliberated on her posthumous name; the Emperor, because the Princess had served Renzong with filial devotion, ordered that she be called Zhuangxiao and posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers debated her posthumous name, the emperor held that she had served Emperor Renzong with filial devotion and ordered the epithet Zhuangxiao, posthumously making her Princess of Qin.

sentences.zh: 徽宗加周、陳國。

translations.literal: Huizong added the states of Zhou and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong added the states of Zhou and Chen to her title.

sentences.zh: 政和改封莊孝明懿大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Under Zhenghe she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Zhuangxiao Mingyi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenghe reign she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Zhuangxiao Mingyi.

sentences.zh: 秦、魯國賢穆明懿大長公主，仁宗皇帝第十女也。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of Qin and Lu, Xianmu Mingyi, was the tenth daughter of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Qin and Lu, posthumously honored as Xianmu Mingyi, was Emperor Renzong's tenth daughter.

sentences.zh: 母曰周貴妃。

translations.literal: Her mother was Honored Consort Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was Honored Consort Zhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐五年，封慶壽，進惠國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiayou, she was enfeoffed as Qingshou and advanced to Princess of the State of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1060 she received the title Qingshou and was promoted to Princess of Hui.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，進許國大長公主。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping, she was advanced to Grand Princess of the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1067 she was raised to Grand Princess of Xu.

sentences.zh: 下嫁吳越忠懿王之曾孫、右領軍衛大將軍錢景臻。

translations.literal: She married down to Qian Jingzhen, great-grandson of King Zhongyi of Wuyue and General-in-Chief of the Right Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: She married Qian Jingzhen, great-grandson of the Wuyue king Zhongyi and a general of the Right Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 改韓、周燕國。

translations.literal: Her title was changed to Princess of Han, Zhou, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Her fiefs were successively redesignated as Han, Zhou, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 徽宗朝，進秦、魏兩國。

translations.literal: Under Huizong's reign, she was advanced to the two states of Qin and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During Huizong's reign she was elevated to the dual titles of Qin and Wei.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，更封令德景行大長帝姬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, she was further enfeoffed as Grand Imperial Princess Lingde Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Lingde Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 靖康二年，諸帝姬北徙，姬以先朝女，金人不知，留於汴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingkang, all imperial princesses were moved north; because she was a daughter of a former reign, the Jurchens did not know of her and she remained at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1127, when the Jurchens marched the imperial princesses north, she alone remained in Bianjing, for as a daughter of an earlier reign they did not recognize her among the court.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，復公主號，改封秦魯國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan, the princess title was restored and she was changed to Princess of Qin and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era her princess title was restored and she was made Princess of Qin and Lu.

sentences.zh: 避地南渡，賊張遇掠其家，中子愕被害。

translations.literal: Fleeing south across the river, the bandit Zhang Yu plundered her household, and her second son E was killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the flight south, the rebel Zhang Yu raided her household and killed her second son, E.

sentences.zh: 公主至揚州朝謁，復避地之閩。

translations.literal: The Princess went to Yangzhou to attend court, then again fled to Min.
translations.idiomatic: She traveled to Yangzhou to pay her respects at court, then fled again to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，自閩至會稽，請入見，因留居焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing, from Min she came to Kuaiji, requested an audience, and therefore remained there.
translations.idiomatic: In 1133 she came from Fujian to Kuaiji, asked for an audience with the emperor, and was invited to remain there.

sentences.zh: 後徙台州。

translations.literal: Later she moved to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: She later moved to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 上以公主行尊年高，甚敬之，每入內，見必先揖。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the Princess in conduct was venerable and advanced in years, greatly respected her; whenever she entered the palace, on seeing her he would bow first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held her in deep respect for her age and dignity; whenever she came to court he bowed to her before she could bow to him.

sentences.zh: 靖康中，戚裏例納節，至是，公主為其子忱請還舊官，上以忱為滬川節度使，仍詔戚裏不得援例。

translations.literal: During Jingkang, imperial affines by precedent surrendered their military commissions; at this time the Princess requested for her son Chen restoration of his former office; the Emperor made Chen Military Commissioner of Huchuan, and still ordered that imperial affines could not cite this as a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang crisis, imperial in-laws had been required to surrender their military commissions; she now petitioned to restore her son Chen's former post, and the emperor appointed him military commissioner of Huchuan while decreeing that no other in-law might cite this as precedent.

sentences.zh: 久之，又為忱請優賜推恩，上重違之，加忱開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: After a long time, she again requested for Chen preferential grants and extended favor; the Emperor, loath to refuse, added for Chen Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Later she again pressed for special favors for Chen; reluctant to refuse her, the emperor made him Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時主有三子，愐、愷非己所出，故獨厚於忱。

translations.literal: At the time the Princess had three sons; Mian and Kai were not born of her, so she favored Chen alone.
translations.idiomatic: She had three sons at the time; Mian and Kai were her stepsons, so she showed special favor only to Chen.

sentences.zh: 上戒之曰：「長主壽考如此，乃仁宗皇帝四十二年深仁厚澤，是以鐘慶於長主。

translations.literal: The Emperor admonished her, saying, "The Grand Princess's longevity is such because of Emperor Renzong's forty-two years of deep benevolence and thick grace—therefore blessings were concentrated upon the Grand Princess.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cautioned her, "Your long life is the fruit of Emperor Renzong's forty-two years of benevolent rule—his grace has gathered upon you alone.

sentences.zh: 長主待遇諸子，宜法仁宗用心之均一。」

translations.literal: In the Grand Princess's treatment of her sons, she should model Renzong's even-handedness of mind."
translations.idiomatic: In how you treat your sons, you should follow Renzong's example of impartial devotion."

sentences.zh: 主感服。

translations.literal: The Princess was moved and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: She was deeply moved and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 薨，年八十六。

translations.literal: She died; she was eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 上輟朝五日，幸其第臨奠，詔子孫皆進官一等。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspended court for five days, visited her residence to mourn, and ordered that all sons and grandsons advance one rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for five days, visited her residence to mourn in person, and ordered that all her descendants be promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 諡曰賢穆。

translations.literal: Her posthumous name was Xianmu.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous epithet Xianmu.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，加諡明懿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Mingyi was added to her posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine years later, Mingyi was added to her posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 袞國大長公主，帝第十一女也。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Yan was the Emperor's eleventh daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Yan was the emperor's eleventh daughter.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，封永壽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiayou, she was enfeoffed as Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1061 she received the title Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 進榮國長公主。

translations.literal: She was advanced to Princess of the State of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to Princess of Rong.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，進邠國大長公主。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping, she was advanced to Grand Princess of the State of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1067 she was raised to Grand Princess of Bin.

sentences.zh: 熙甯九年，改魯國。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xining, her title was changed to the State of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1076 her fief was redesignated as the State of Lu.

sentences.zh: 下嫁左領軍衛大將軍曹詩。

translations.literal: She married down to Cao Shi, General-in-Chief of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: She married Cao Shi, a general of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 主性儉節，于池台苑囿一無所增飭。

translations.literal: The Princess by nature was frugal; to pools, terraces, gardens, and parks she added nothing.
translations.idiomatic: She was frugal by nature and never enlarged her pools, terraces, or gardens.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，旱，曹族以主生日將盛具為壽，主曰：「上方損膳徹樂，吾何心能安。」

translations.literal: In the tenth summer, during drought, the Cao clan because of the Princess's birthday were about to set out lavish provisions for celebration; the Princess said, "Above, the court is reducing meals and withdrawing music—how can my heart be at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of her tenth year, during a drought, the Cao clan prepared a lavish birthday feast; she said, "The court is cutting back meals and suspending music—how could I enjoy such a celebration?"

sentences.zh: 悉屏之。

translations.literal: She had them all removed.
translations.idiomatic: She had everything sent away.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年薨，年二十四，追封荊國，諡賢懿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng she died, aged twenty-four; she was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Jing, with the posthumous name Xianyi.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1083 at twenty-four; posthumously she was made Princess of Jing with the epithet Xianyi.

sentences.zh: 遷其二子曄、旼皆領團練使。

translations.literal: Her two sons Ye and Min were both promoted to command regimental training.
translations.idiomatic: Her two sons Ye and Min were both promoted to regimental training commissioners.

sentences.zh: 徽宗追封袞國，又改賢懿恭穆大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Huizong posthumously enfeoffed her as Princess of Yan and further changed her to Grand Imperial Princess Xianyi Gongmu.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong posthumously made her Princess of Yan and later retitled her Grand Imperial Princess Xianyi Gongmu.

sentences.zh: 燕、舒國大長公主，帝第十二女也。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of Yan and Shu was the Emperor's twelfth daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Yan and Shu was the emperor's twelfth daughter.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，封寶壽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiayou, she was enfeoffed as Baoshou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1061 she received the title Baoshou.

sentences.zh: 八年，進順國長公主。

translations.literal: In the eighth year she was advanced to Princess of the State of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year she was promoted to Princess of Shun.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，進冀國大長公主。，

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping, she was advanced to Grand Princess of the State of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In 1067 she was raised to Grand Princess of Ji.

sentences.zh: 改魏國，下嫁開州團練使郭獻卿。

translations.literal: Her title was changed to the State of Wei and she married down to Guo Xianqing, regimentation commissioner of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: She was redesignated Princess of Wei and married Guo Xianqing, regimentation commissioner of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 上，進楚國。

translations.literal: She was advanced to Princess of the State of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to Princess of Chu.

sentences.zh: 徽宗改吳國，進吳、越國，改秦、袞國。

translations.literal: Huizong changed her title to the State of Wu, advanced her to Wu and Yue, and changed her to the states of Qin and Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong redesignated her Princess of Wu, then elevated her to Wu and Yue, and later to Qin and Gun.

sentences.zh: 薨，追封燕、舒國，諡懿穆，復改懿穆大長帝姬。

translations.literal: She died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Yan and Shu, with the posthumous name Yimu, then further changed to Grand Imperial Princess Yimu.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she was posthumously made Princess of Yan and Shu, with the epithet Yimu, and later retitled Grand Imperial Princess Yimu.

sentences.zh: 英宗四女

translations.literal: Four Daughters of Yingzong
translations.idiomatic: The Four Daughters of Emperor Yingzong

sentences.zh: 英宗四女。

translations.literal: Four Daughters of Yingzong
translations.idiomatic: The Four Daughters of Emperor Yingzong

sentences.zh: 舒國公主，早亡。

translations.literal: The Princess of the State of Shu died young.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Shu died young.

sentences.zh: 魏、楚國大長公主，帝長女。，

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of Wei and Chu was the Emperor's eldest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Wei and Chu was the emperor's eldest daughter.

sentences.zh: 封德寧。，

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Denning.
translations.idiomatic: She received the title Denning.

sentences.zh: 進封徐國，下嫁左衛將軍王師約。

translations.literal: She was advanced to Princess of the State of Xu and married down to Wang Shiyue, General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to Princess of Xu and married Wang Shiyue, a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，進陳國長公主。

translations.literal: In the fourth year she was advanced to Princess of the State of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year she was raised to Princess of Chen.

sentences.zh: 薨，追封燕國大長公主，諡惠和。，

translations.literal: She died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Yan, with the posthumous name Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she was posthumously made Grand Princess of Yan with the epithet Huihe.

sentences.zh: 追封秦國。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made Princess of Qin.

sentences.zh: 徽宗追封魏國，加韓、魏國，又改惠和大長帝姬。

translations.literal: Huizong posthumously enfeoffed her as Princess of Wei, added Han and Wei, and further changed her to Grand Imperial Princess Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong posthumously made her Princess of Wei, added the dual title of Han and Wei, and retitled her Grand Imperial Princess Huihe.

sentences.zh: 魏國大長公主，帝第二女，母曰宣仁聖烈皇后。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of the State of Wei was the Emperor's second daughter; her mother was Empress Xuanren Shengli.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Wei was the emperor's second daughter; her mother was Empress Xuanren Shengli.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐八年，封寶安公主。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiayou, she was enfeoffed as Princess of Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1063 she was made Princess of Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，進舒國長公主，改蜀國，下嫁左衛將軍王詵。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended, she was advanced to Princess of the State of Shu, changed to the State of Shu, and married down to Wang Shen, General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, she was promoted to Princess of Shu, redesignated Princess of Shu, and married Wang Shen, a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 詵母盧寡居，主處之近舍，日致膳羞。

translations.literal: Shen's mother Lu lived as a widow; the Princess lodged her in a nearby residence and daily sent food and delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen's mother, Lady Lu, lived alone as a widow; the princess housed her nearby and sent meals every day.

sentences.zh: 盧病，自和湯劑以進。

translations.literal: When Lu fell ill, the Princess herself mixed medicinal decoctions to present to her.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Lu fell ill, she personally prepared medicines for her.

sentences.zh: 帝厚于姊妹，故主第池籞服玩極其華縟。

translations.literal: The Emperor was generous toward his sisters, so the Princess's residence, pools, parks, garments, and curios were extremely lavish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lavished affection on his sisters, and her mansion, gardens, and furnishings were accordingly sumptuous.

sentences.zh: 主以不得日侍宣仁于寶慈宮，居常悒然。

translations.literal: Because the Princess could not daily attend Xuanren at Baoci Palace, she was habitually melancholy.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to visit Empress Xuanren daily at Baoci Palace, she was often despondent.

sentences.zh: 間遇旱暵，帝降損以禱，主亦如之，曰：「我奉賜皆出公上，固應同其傈戚。」

translations.literal: Whenever drought occurred, the Emperor reduced his meals to pray; the Princess did likewise, saying, "My allowances all come from the public treasury—I should surely share his anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: During droughts, when the emperor cut back his meals to pray for rain, she did the same, saying, "Everything I receive comes from the state—I ought to share his distress."

sentences.zh: 帝居慈聖光獻皇后喪，毀甚，主曰：「吾與上同體，視此亦復保聊！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor observed mourning for Empress Cisheng Guangxian and was utterly devastated, the Princess said, "I share one body with Your Majesty—how can I alone remain at ease in this!"
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for Empress Cisheng Guangxian, when the emperor was utterly prostrate with grief, she said, "We are of one flesh—how can I alone find comfort in music!"

sentences.zh: 立散遣歌舞三十輩。，

translations.literal: She immediately dismissed thirty troupes of singers and dancers.
translations.idiomatic: She at once dismissed thirty companies of singers and dancers.

sentences.zh: 病篤。

translations.literal: She grew gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: She fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 主性不妒忌，王詵以是自恣，嘗貶官。

translations.literal: The Princess was not jealous by nature; Wang Shen therefore indulged himself and was once demoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was not jealous by nature; Wang Shen took advantage of this and was once demoted.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝命還詵官，以慰主意。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor ordered Shen's office restored to comfort the Princess.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the emperor ordered Wang Shen's office restored to comfort her.

sentences.zh: 太后臨問，已不省，后慟哭，久稍能言，自訴必不起，相持而泣。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager came to inquire after her; she was already unconscious. The Empress wept bitterly; after a long while she could speak a little, saying she would surely not recover, and they embraced and wept together.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager came to see her, but she was already unconscious. The empress wept bitterly; after a long while she could speak a little, said she would not recover, and they embraced and wept.

sentences.zh: 帝繼至，自為診脈，親持粥食之，主強為帝盡食。

translations.literal: The Emperor then arrived, personally felt her pulse, and held porridge for her to eat; the Princess forced herself to finish it all for the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then arrived, felt her pulse himself, and fed her porridge with his own hands; she forced herself to eat it all for his sake.

sentences.zh: 賜金帛六千，且問所須，但謝復詵官而已。

translations.literal: He bestowed six thousand in gold and silks and asked what she needed, but she only thanked him for restoring Shen's office.
translations.idiomatic: He gave her six thousand in gold and silks and asked what she wished for, but she thanked him only for restoring Wang Shen's office.

sentences.zh: 明日薨，年三十。

translations.literal: The next day she died, aged thirty.
translations.idiomatic: She died the next day at the age of thirty.

sentences.zh: 帝未上食即駕往，望第門而哭，輟朝五日。

translations.literal: Before taking his morning meal the Emperor drove there at once, wept on seeing the gate of her residence, and suspended court for five days.
translations.idiomatic: Before breakfast the emperor drove there at once, wept on seeing her gate, and suspended court for five days.

sentences.zh: 追封越國，諡賢慧。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Yue, with the posthumous name Xianhui.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made Princess of Yue with the epithet Xianhui.

sentences.zh: 後進封大長公主，累改秦、荊、魏三國。

translations.literal: Later she was advanced to Grand Princess and successively changed to the three states of Qin, Jing, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later she was raised to Grand Princess and successively redesignated Qin, Jing, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 主好讀古文，喜筆劄，賙恤族黨，中外稱賢。

translations.literal: The Princess loved reading ancient texts, delighted in letters, relieved and aided her clan, and was called virtuous within and without.
translations.idiomatic: She loved classical prose, enjoyed correspondence, supported her kin generously, and was praised as virtuous throughout the court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 詵不矜細行，至與妾奸主旁，妾數抵戾主。

translations.literal: Shen did not restrain minor conduct; he even committed adultery with a concubine beside the Princess, and the concubine repeatedly offended the Princess.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen was careless in small matters; he even lay with a concubine in the princess's presence, and the woman repeatedly insulted her.

sentences.zh: 薨後，乳母訴之，帝命窮治，杖八妝以配兵。

translations.literal: After she died, her wet nurse reported this; the Emperor ordered a full investigation and had eight maids beaten and assigned to soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: After her death, her wet nurse reported the affair; the emperor ordered a full inquiry and had eight maids flogged and married off to soldiers.

sentences.zh: 既葬，謫詵均州。

translations.literal: After the burial, Shen was banished to Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After her burial, Wang Shen was exiled to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 子彥弼，生三歲卒。

translations.literal: Her son Yanbi died at the age of three.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Yanbi died at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 韓、魏國大長公主，帝第三女，與魏國同生。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of Han and Wei was the Emperor's third daughter, born together with the Princess of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Han and Wei was the emperor's third daughter, a twin of the Princess of Wei.

sentences.zh: 始封壽康公主，改祁國、衛國，下嫁張敦禮。

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess Shoukang, changed to the states of Qi and Wei, and married down to Zhang Dunli.
translations.idiomatic: She was first made Princess Shoukang, redesignated Princess of Qi and Wei, and married Zhang Dunli.

sentences.zh: 進冀國大長公主，改秦、越、楚國，加今封。

translations.literal: She was advanced to Grand Princess of the State of Ji, changed to the states of Qin, Yue, and Chu, and given her present title.
translations.idiomatic: She was raised to Grand Princess of Ji, successively made Princess of Qin, Yue, and Chu, and given her present dual title.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，改賢德懿行大長帝姬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, she was changed to Grand Imperial Princess Xiande Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 she was retitled Grand Imperial Princess Xiande Yixing.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: She died.
translations.idiomatic: She died.

sentences.zh: 神宗十女

translations.literal: Ten Daughters of Shenzong
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Daughters of Emperor Shenzong

sentences.zh: 楚國、鄆國、潞國、刑國、邠國、袞國六公主，皆早薨。

translations.literal: The six princesses of Chu, Yun, Lu, Xing, Bin, and Gun all died early.
translations.idiomatic: The six princesses of Chu, Yun, Lu, Xing, Bin, and Gun all died young.

sentences.zh: 周國長公主，帝長女也。

translations.literal: The Princess of the State of Zhou was the Emperor's eldest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Zhou was the emperor's eldest daughter.

sentences.zh: 母曰欽聖憲肅皇后。

translations.literal: Her mother was Empress Qinsheng Xiansu.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was Empress Qinsheng Xiansu.

sentences.zh: 封延禧公主。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Princess Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: She was made Princess Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 生而警悟，自羈丱習嗜宛如成人。

translations.literal: From birth she was quick-witted; from childhood in restraint her tastes and habits were like an adult's.
translations.idiomatic: She was precocious from birth; even as a small child her tastes and habits were those of an adult.

sentences.zh: 年十二卒，帝后皆變服哀送。

translations.literal: At the age of twelve she died; the Emperor and Empress both changed garments and mournfully escorted her.
translations.idiomatic: She died at twelve; the emperor and empress both donned mourning dress and escorted her bier in grief.

sentences.zh: 追贈燕國。

translations.literal: She was posthumously granted the State of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made Princess of Yan.

sentences.zh: 元符末，改封周國。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfu, her title was changed to the State of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanfu era she was redesignated Princess of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 唐國長公主，帝第三女也。

translations.literal: The Princess of the State of Tang was the Emperor's third daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Tang was the emperor's third daughter.

sentences.zh: 始封淑壽公主。

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess Shushou.
translations.idiomatic: She was first made Princess Shushou.

sentences.zh: 初，帝念韓琦功德，欲與為婚姻，故哲宗緣先帝，以主降琦之子嘉彥。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor, mindful of Han Qi's merit and virtue, wished to ally with him by marriage; therefore Zhezong, following the former emperor, had the Princess marry Qi's son Jiayan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering Han Qi's service, wished to ally with him by marriage; Zhezong therefore followed his predecessor and had the princess marry Qi's son Jiayan.

sentences.zh: 曆封溫、曹、冀、雍、越、燕六國。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed in succession through the six states of Wen, Cao, Ji, Yong, Yue, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Her fiefs were successively Wen, Cao, Ji, Yong, Yue, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 薨，追封唐國長公主。

translations.literal: She died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of the State of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she was posthumously made Princess of Tang.

sentences.zh: 潭國賢孝長公主，帝第四女也。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess of Tan, Xianxiao, was the Emperor's fourth daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess of Tan, posthumously Xianxiao, was the emperor's fourth daughter.

sentences.zh: 母曰宋貴妃。

translations.literal: Her mother was Honored Consort Song.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was Honored Consort Song.

sentences.zh: 始封康國。，

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: She was first made Princess of Kang.

sentences.zh: 下嫁王遇。

translations.literal: She married down to Wang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wang Yu.

sentences.zh: 曆韓、魯、陳、鄆四國。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed in succession through the four states of Han, Lu, Chen, and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Her fiefs were successively Han, Lu, Chen, and Yun.

sentences.zh: 薨，追加封諡。

translations.literal: She died and was further granted enfeoffment and a posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she received additional enfeoffment and a posthumous epithet.

sentences.zh: 徐國長公主，帝幼女也。

translations.literal: The Princess of the State of Xu was the Emperor's youngest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Xu was the emperor's youngest daughter.

sentences.zh: 母曰欽成皇后。

translations.literal: Her mother was Empress Qincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was Empress Qincheng.

sentences.zh: 始封慶國，進益、冀、蜀、徐四國。

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess of Qing, then advanced through the four states of Yi, Ji, Shu, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: She was first made Princess of Qing, then successively elevated through Yi, Ji, Shu, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 年及笄，猶處聖瑞宮。

translations.literal: Though she reached marriageable age, she still resided at Shengrui Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Even after coming of age she continued to live in Shengrui Palace.

sentences.zh: 侍母疾，晝夜不暫去，藥餌非經手弗以進。

translations.literal: Attending her mother's illness, day and night she never left for a moment; medicines and food she would not allow to be presented unless they had passed through her own hands.
translations.idiomatic: While nursing her mother she never left her side day or night, and would allow no medicine or food to be given unless she had prepared it herself.

sentences.zh: 迨疾革，號慟屢絕，左右不忍視。

translations.literal: When the illness became critical, she wailed and collapsed repeatedly; those beside her could not bear to look.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother grew critically ill, she wailed until she fainted again and again; her attendants could scarcely bear to watch.

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，下嫁鄭王潘美之曾孫意。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, she married down to Yi, great-grandson of Prince Zheng Pan Mei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1104 she married Yi, great-grandson of Prince Zheng Pan Mei.

sentences.zh: 事姑修婦道。

translations.literal: She served her mother-in-law and cultivated the way of a wife.
translations.idiomatic: She served her mother-in-law devotedly and observed every propriety of a daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 潘故大族，夫黨數千百人，賓接皆盡禮，無裏外言。

translations.literal: The Pan were an old great clan; her husband's kin numbered in the hundreds and thousands; in receiving guests she observed full ritual, with no talk of inside or outside.
translations.idiomatic: The Pan were an eminent clan with hundreds of in-laws; she received every guest with perfect courtesy and never gossiped about household affairs.

sentences.zh: 志向沖淡，服玩不為紛華，歲時簡嬉遊，十年間惟一適西池而已。

translations.literal: Her aspirations were plain; garments and curios were not made gaudy; at the seasons she kept merrymaking simple; in ten years she went only once to the Western Pond.
translations.idiomatic: She lived simply, shunning lavish dress and ornaments, kept festivities restrained, and in ten years visited the Western Pond only once.

sentences.zh: 再生子，不成而死，滕妾得女，拊視如己出。

translations.literal: She bore another son, who did not survive and died; a concubine of Teng bore a daughter, whom she reared and regarded as her own.
translations.idiomatic: She bore another son who did not live; when a concubine bore a daughter, she reared the child as her own.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，改稱柔惠帝姬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, she was renamed Imperial Princess Rouhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 she was retitled Imperial Princess Rouhui.

sentences.zh: 五年薨，年三十一，追封賢靜長帝姬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year she died, aged thirty-one; she was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Imperial Princess Xianjing.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1115 at thirty-one and was posthumously made Grand Imperial Princess Xianjing.

sentences.zh: 哲宗四女

translations.literal: Four Daughters of Zhezong
translations.idiomatic: The Four Daughters of Emperor Zhezong

sentences.zh: 哲宗四女。

translations.literal: Four Daughters of Zhezong
translations.idiomatic: The Four Daughters of Emperor Zhezong

sentences.zh: 鄧國、揚國二公主，早亡。

translations.literal: The Princesses of Deng and Yang both died young.
translations.idiomatic: The princesses of Deng and Yang both died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 陳國公主，始封德康公主，進瀛國、榮國。，

translations.literal: The Princess of the State of Chen was first enfeoffed as Princess Dekang and advanced to the states of Ying and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Chen was first made Princess Dekang, then promoted to Ying and Rong.

sentences.zh: 下嫁石端禮，徙陳國。

translations.literal: She married down to Shi Duanli and was transferred to the State of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: She married Shi Duanli and was redesignated Princess of Chen.

sentences.zh: 改淑和帝姬。

translations.literal: She was changed to Imperial Princess Shuhe.
translations.idiomatic: She was retitled Imperial Princess Shuhe.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: She died.
translations.idiomatic: She died.

sentences.zh: 秦國康懿長公主，帝第三女也。

translations.literal: The Princess of Qin, Kangyi, was the Emperor's third daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Qin, posthumously Kangyi, was the emperor's third daughter.

sentences.zh: 始封康懿，進嘉國、慶國。

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Kangyi, then advanced to the states of Jia and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: She was first titled Kangyi, then promoted to Jia and Qing.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，改韓國公主，出降潘正夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, she was changed to Princess of Han and married out to Pan Zhengfu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1112 she was made Princess of Han and married Pan Zhengfu.

sentences.zh: 改淑慎帝姬。

translations.literal: She was changed to Imperial Princess Shushen.
translations.idiomatic: She was retitled Imperial Princess Shushen.

sentences.zh: 靖康末，與賢德懿行大長公主俱以先朝女留於汴。

translations.literal: At the end of Jingkang, together with the Grand Imperial Princess Xiande Yixing, as daughters of a former reign they remained at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jingkang crisis, she and the Grand Imperial Princess Xiande Yixing, as daughters of an earlier reign, were left behind in Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，復公主號，改封吳國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan, the princess title was restored and she was changed to Princess of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era her princess title was restored and she was made Princess of Wu.

sentences.zh: 覲上於越，以玉管筆、小玉山、奇畫為獻，上溫辭卻之。

translations.literal: She had an audience with the Emperor at Yue and presented a jade-tube brush, a small jade mountain, and rare paintings; the Emperor gently declined them.
translations.idiomatic: When she had an audience in Yue, she offered a jade brush, a miniature jade mountain, and fine paintings; the emperor courteously refused them.

sentences.zh: 避地至婺州。

translations.literal: Fleeing the turmoil, she went to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: She fled south to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入見，其子堯卿等五人各進官一等。

translations.literal: On entering audience, her sons Yaoqing and four others were each advanced one rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: On her audience at court, her sons Yaoqing and four others were each promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 主奏言：「祖宗以來，駙馬都尉石保吉、魏咸信、柴宗慶皆除使相。

translations.literal: The Princess memorialized, saying, "Since the founding ancestors, the imperial sons-in-law Shi Baoji, Wei Xianxin, and Chai Zongqing have all been appointed military commissioners and chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The princess memorialized: "Since the founding of the dynasty, imperial sons-in-law Shi Baoji, Wei Xianxin, and Chai Zongqing have all been made military commissioners and chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 今正夫曆事四朝，在汴京曾建議迎陛下，至杭州又言禁衛未集，預宜防變，乞除開府。」

translations.literal: Now Zhengfu has served through four reigns; at Bianjing he once proposed welcoming Your Majesty, and at Hangzhou he said the palace guard was not yet assembled and foresaw the need to guard against unrest. I beg that he be granted the office of Grand Preceptor of the Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhengfu has served four reigns. At Bianjing he urged welcoming Your Majesty; at Hangzhou he warned that the palace guard was not yet assembled and that unrest should be guarded against. I beg that he be granted the office of Grand Preceptor of the Palace."

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 八年再入見。

translations.literal: In the eighth year she entered audience again.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later she had another audience.

sentences.zh: 留宮中三日。

translations.literal: She remained in the palace for three days.
translations.idiomatic: She stayed in the palace for three days.

sentences.zh: 時極暑，上每正衣冠對之飲食，又為正夫求恩數，上曰：「官爵豈可私與人，況今日多事，未暇及此。」

translations.literal: It was extremely hot; the Emperor each time dressed formally to dine with her, and again sought favors for Zhengfu. The Emperor said, "How can offices and ranks be given privately to others? Moreover, today there are many affairs, and there is no leisure for this."
translations.idiomatic: In extreme summer heat the emperor dressed formally whenever he dined with her. When she again sought favors for Zhengfu, he said, "How can offices and ranks be granted as private gifts? And with so many urgent affairs today, I have no time for this."

sentences.zh: 時趙鼎當國，方論群臣紹述之奸，頗抑正夫。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Ding held power and was denouncing the factional evils of the Shaoshu partisans, and he greatly restrained Zhengfu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhao Ding was in power, denouncing the Shaoshu faction, and he greatly restrained Zhengfu.

sentences.zh: 鼎去位，正夫始得開府之命。

translations.literal: When Ding left office, Zhengfu at last received appointment as Grand Preceptor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Ding left office, Zhengfu finally received appointment as Grand Preceptor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉一正言其非舊制，恐援例者多，乃詔：「哲宗惟正夫為近親，余人毋得援。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Yizheng said this was not the old regulation and feared many would cite it as precedent; an edict thereupon stated, "Of Zhezong's close kin, only Zhengfu may be cited; others may not follow this example."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Yizheng objected that this was not precedent and feared many would cite it; an edict declared, "Of Zhezong's close kin, only Zhengfu may be cited as precedent; no one else may follow this example."

sentences.zh: 顯仁太后歸，主同秦、魯國大長公主迎于道。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xianren returned, the Princess together with the Grand Princesses of Qin and Lu welcomed her on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xianren returned, the princess joined the Grand Princesses of Qin and Lu in welcoming her along the route.

sentences.zh: 十九年，又入朝。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year she again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year she came to court again.

sentences.zh: 子長卿、粹卿、端卿皆自團練使升觀察使，從所請也。

translations.literal: Her sons Changqing, Cuiqing, and Duanqing were all advanced from regimental training commissioners to regional inspectors, as she had requested.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons Changqing, Cuiqing, and Duanqing were all promoted from regimental training commissioners to regional inspectors, as she had requested.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，進封秦國大長公主。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong acceded, she was advanced to Grand Princess of the State of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, she was promoted to Grand Princess of Qin.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡康懿。

translations.literal: She died and was granted the posthumous name Kangyi.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she received the posthumous epithet Kangyi.

sentences.zh: 主在日，正夫官至少傅，封和國公；

translations.literal: While the Princess lived, Zhengfu's office reached Junior Tutor and he was enfeoffed as Duke of He;
translations.idiomatic: During her lifetime, Zhengfu rose to Junior Tutor and was made Duke of He;

sentences.zh: 溫卿甯國軍承宣使，長卿甯江軍承宣使，端卿昭信軍承宣使，清卿容州觀察使，墨卿、才卿並帶團練使，其盛如此。

translations.literal: Wenqing was Military Commissioner of Ningguo Army; Changqing of Ningjiang Army; Duanqing of Zhaoxin Army; Qingqing Regional Inspector of Rongzhou; Moqing and Caiqing both held regimental training commissions—their splendor was such.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing became commissioner of the Ningguo army; Changqing of the Ningjiang army; Duanqing of the Zhaoxin army; Qingqing inspector of Rongzhou; Moqing and Caiqing both held regimental training posts—the family's favor reached such heights.

sentences.zh: 正夫薨於紹興二十二年，贈太傅。

translations.literal: Zhengfu died in the twenty-second year of Shaoxing and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu died in 1152 and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 徽宗三十四女

translations.literal: Thirty-Four Daughters of Huizong
translations.idiomatic: The Thirty-Four Daughters of Emperor Huizong

sentences.zh: 徽宗三十四女。

translations.literal: Thirty-Four Daughters of Huizong
translations.idiomatic: The Thirty-Four Daughters of Emperor Huizong

sentences.zh: 政和三年，改公主號為帝姬，國號易以美名，二字。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, the princess title was changed to Imperial Princess; state designations were replaced with elegant two-character names.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 the title "princess" was replaced by "imperial princess," and state names were exchanged for elegant two-character epithets.

sentences.zh: 嘉德帝姬，六月，封德慶公主。

translations.literal: Imperial Princess Jiade, in the sixth month, was enfeoffed as Princess Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Princess Jiade, in the sixth month, was made Princess Deqing.

sentences.zh: 改封嘉福，尋改號帝姬，再封嘉德。

translations.literal: Her title was changed to Jiafu; soon the Imperial Princess title was adopted and she was again enfeoffed as Jiade.
translations.idiomatic: She was redesignated Jiafu, soon received the imperial princess title, and was again made Jiade.

sentences.zh: 下嫁左衛將軍曾夤。

translations.literal: She married down to Zeng Yin, General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: She married Zeng Yin, a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 榮德帝姬，初封永慶公主，改封榮福。

translations.literal: Imperial Princess Rongde was first enfeoffed as Princess Yongqing, then changed to Rongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Princess Rongde was first made Princess Yongqing, then redesignated Rongfu.

sentences.zh: 尋改號帝姬，再封榮德。

translations.literal: Soon the Imperial Princess title was adopted and she was again enfeoffed as Rongde.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she received the imperial princess title and was again made Rongde.

sentences.zh: 下嫁左衛將軍曹晟。

translations.literal: She married down to Cao Sheng, General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: She married Cao Sheng, a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 順淑帝姬，初封順慶公主。

translations.literal: Imperial Princess Shunshu was first enfeoffed as Princess Shunqing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Princess Shunshu was first made Princess Shunqing.

sentences.zh: 薨，追封益國。

translations.literal: She died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she was posthumously made Princess of Yi.

sentences.zh: 及改帝姬號，追封順淑。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Princess title was adopted, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Shunshu.
translations.idiomatic: When the new title was introduced, she was posthumously made Imperial Princess Shunshu.

sentences.zh: 安德帝姬，初封淑慶公主，改封安福。

translations.literal: Imperial Princess Ande was first enfeoffed as Princess Shuqing and changed to Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Princess Ande was first made Princess Shuqing, then redesignated Anfu.

sentences.zh: 尋改號帝姬，再封安德。

translations.literal: Soon the Imperial Princess title was adopted and she was again enfeoffed as Ande.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she received the imperial princess title and was again made Ande.

sentences.zh: 下嫁左衛將軍邦光。

translations.literal: She married down to Bang Guang, General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: She married Bang Guang, a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 茂德帝姬，初封延慶公主，改封康福。

translations.literal: Imperial Princess Maode was first enfeoffed as Princess Yanqing and changed to Kangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Princess Maode was first made Princess Yanqing, then redesignated Kangfu.

sentences.zh: 尋改號帝姬，再封茂德。

translations.literal: Soon the Imperial Princess title was adopted and she was again enfeoffed as Maode.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she received the imperial princess title and was again made Maode.

sentences.zh: 下嫁宣和殿待制蔡鞗。

translations.literal: She married down to Cai Biao, Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Xuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: She married Cai Biao, awaiting draftsman of the Hall of Xuanhe.

sentences.zh: 壽淑帝姬，初封壽慶公主。

translations.literal: Imperial Princess Shoushu was first enfeoffed as Princess Shouqing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Princess Shoushu was first made Princess Shouqing.

sentences.zh: 薨，追封豫國。

translations.literal: She died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she was posthumously made Princess of Yu.

sentences.zh: 及改帝姬號，追封壽淑。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Princess title was adopted, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Shoushu.
translations.idiomatic: When the new title was introduced, she was posthumously made Imperial Princess Shoushu.

sentences.zh: 安淑帝姬，初封安慶公主，改封隆福。

translations.literal: Imperial Princess Anshu was first enfeoffed as Princess Anqing, then changed to Longfu.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Princess Anshu was first made Princess Anqing, then redesignated Longfu.

sentences.zh: 薨，追封蜀國。

translations.literal: She died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she was posthumously made Princess of Shu.

sentences.zh: 及改帝姬號，追封安淑。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Princess title was adopted, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Anshu.
translations.idiomatic: When the new title was introduced, she was posthumously made Imperial Princess Anshu.
