sentences.zh: 崇德帝姬，初封和慶公主，改封崇福。

translations.literal: Imperial Princess Chongde was first enfeoffed as Princess Heqing and changed to Chongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Princess Chongde was first made Princess Heqing, then redesignated Chongfu.

sentences.zh: 尋改帝姬號。

translations.literal: Soon the Imperial Princess title was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she received the imperial princess title.

sentences.zh: 下嫁左衛將軍曹湜。

translations.literal: She married down to Cao Shi, General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: She married Cao Shi, a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 再封崇德。

translations.literal: She was again enfeoffed as Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: She was again made Chongde.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: She died.
translations.idiomatic: She died.

sentences.zh: 柔福在五國城，適徐還而薨。

translations.literal: Roufu was in the Five States Fortress; she married Xu Huan and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Roufu was held in the Five States Fortress, where she married Xu Huan and died.

sentences.zh: 靜善遂伏誅。

translations.literal: Jingshan was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan was then put to death.

sentences.zh: 柔福薨在紹興十一年，從梓宮來者以其骨至，葬之，追封和國長公主。

translations.literal: Roufu died in the eleventh year of Shaoxing; those who came with the imperial coffin brought her bones; she was buried and posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of He.
translations.idiomatic: Roufu died in 1141; when the imperial coffin procession returned, her remains were brought back, interred, and she was posthumously made Princess of He.

sentences.zh: 孝宗二女

translations.literal: Two Daughters of Xiaozong
translations.idiomatic: The Two Daughters of Emperor Xiaozong

sentences.zh: 孝宗二女：長嘉國公主，紹興二十四年，封碩人，進永嘉郡主，三十二年卒。

translations.literal: Xiaozong had two daughters: the elder, Princess of Jia, in the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing was enfeoffed as Shuren, advanced to Princess of Yongjia, and died in the thirty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong had two daughters: the elder became Princess of Jia; in 1154 she was made Shuren, then Princess of Yongjia, and died in 1162.

sentences.zh: 詔以醫官李師克等屬吏，孝宗時居東宮，奏：「臣女幼而多疾，不宜罪醫。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered the medical officer Li Shike and others handed over to judicial officials; when Xiaozong was in the Eastern Palace he memorialized: "My daughter from childhood has been often ill—it is not fitting to punish the physicians."
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for prosecuting the physician Li Shike and others; when Xiaozong was crown prince he wrote, "My daughter has been sickly since childhood—the physicians should not be punished."

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，贈嘉國公主。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao, she was posthumously granted the title Princess of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1166 she was posthumously made Princess of Jia.

sentences.zh: 次女生五月而夭，未及封。

translations.literal: The younger daughter died at five months and was not enfeoffed in time.
translations.idiomatic: The younger daughter died at five months before she could receive a title.

sentences.zh: 光宗三女

translations.literal: Three Daughters of Guangzong
translations.idiomatic: The Three Daughters of Emperor Guangzong

sentences.zh: 文安郡主，光宗長女也；次女封和政郡主；季女封齊安郡主。

translations.literal: Princess of Wen'an was Guangzong's eldest daughter; the second daughter was enfeoffed as Princess of Hezheng; the youngest as Princess of Qi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Wen'an was Emperor Guangzong's eldest daughter; his second daughter was made Princess of Hezheng and his youngest Princess of Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 皆早卒。

translations.literal: All died young.
translations.idiomatic: All three died young.

sentences.zh: 並追贈公主。

translations.literal: They were all posthumously enfeoffed as princesses.
translations.idiomatic: They were all posthumously granted princess titles.

sentences.zh: 魏惠獻王一女

translations.literal: One Daughter of Prince Weihui Xian
translations.idiomatic: The Daughter of Prince Weihui Xian

sentences.zh: 安康郡主，魏惠獻王女也。

translations.literal: Princess of Ankang was a daughter of Prince Weihui Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Ankang was the daughter of Prince Weihui Xian.

sentences.zh: 初封永寧郡主，改封通義。

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess of Yongning, then changed to Tongyi.
translations.idiomatic: She was first made Princess of Yongning, then redesignated Princess of Tongyi.

sentences.zh: 以父遺表，遂升安康。

translations.literal: On the basis of her father's testamentary memorial, she was then advanced to Ankang.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of her father's final memorial, she was elevated to Princess of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 歸殿前司前軍統領羅忠信子良臣。

translations.literal: She married Liangchen, son of Luo Zhongxin, commander of the Vanguard of the Palace Front Command.
translations.idiomatic: She married Liangchen, son of Luo Zhongxin, a commander of the Palace Front Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 詔王府主管鄧從義諭旨：「皇女孫郡主宜執婦道，務成肅雍之德，毋敢或違。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered the prince's residence supervisor Deng Congyi to convey the instruction: "The imperial granddaughter the Princess should uphold the way of a wife, strive to achieve dignified harmony, and dare not violate this in the least."
translations.idiomatic: An edict instructed the prince's household supervisor Deng Congyi to tell her, "As the emperor's granddaughter, you must observe every duty of a wife and cultivate a household of dignity and harmony—do not fall short in the least."

sentences.zh: 賜申第居之。

translations.literal: A residence in Shen district was granted for her to live in.
translations.idiomatic: She was given a mansion in the Shen quarter to live in.

sentences.zh: 良臣以恩轉秉義郎，除閣門祗候官。

translations.literal: Liangchen by grace was transferred to Gentleman of Integrity and Righteousness and appointed Attendant of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial favor Liangchen was promoted to Gentleman of Integrity and appointed palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年，郡主薨，年三十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi, the Princess died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 1205 at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 甯宗一女

translations.literal: One Daughter of Ningzong
translations.idiomatic: The Daughter of Emperor Ningzong

sentences.zh: 祁國公主，甯宗女也。

translations.literal: The Princess of the State of Qi was a daughter of Ningzong.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Qi was a daughter of Emperor Ningzong.

sentences.zh: 生六月而薨，追封祁國。

translations.literal: She died at six months and was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: She died at six months and was posthumously made Princess of Qi.

sentences.zh: 理宗一女

translations.literal: One Daughter of Lizong
translations.idiomatic: The Daughter of Emperor Lizong

sentences.zh: 周、漢國公主，理宗女也。

translations.literal: The Princess of Zhou and Han was a daughter of Lizong.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Zhou and Han was a daughter of Emperor Lizong.

sentences.zh: 母賈貴妃，早薨。

translations.literal: Her mother was Honored Consort Jia, who died early.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother, Honored Consort Jia, died young.

sentences.zh: 帝無子，公主生而甚鍾愛。

translations.literal: The Emperor had no sons; from birth the Princess was deeply cherished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no sons, and from her birth he doted on the princess.

sentences.zh: 初封瑞國公主，改升國。

translations.literal: She was first enfeoffed as Princess of Rui, then changed to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: She was first made Princess of Rui, then redesignated Princess of Sheng.

sentences.zh: 開慶初，公主年及笄，詔議選尚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiqing, when the Princess reached marriageable age, an edict ordered discussion of selecting a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiqing era, when she came of age, an edict was issued to choose a husband for her.

sentences.zh: 宰臣請用唐太宗降士人故事，欲以進士第一人尚主，遂取周震炎。

translations.literal: The chief ministers requested using the precedent of Emperor Taizong of Tang marrying her to a scholar, wishing to have the top jinshi graduate marry the Princess; Zhou Zhenyan was accordingly chosen.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers proposed following Tang Taizong's precedent of marrying a princess to a scholar and wished to give her to the top jinshi graduate; Zhou Zhenyan was selected.

sentences.zh: 廷謝日，公主適從屏內窺見，意頗不懌，帝微知之。

translations.literal: On the day of the court thanksgiving audience, the Princess happened to peer from behind a screen and was rather displeased; the Emperor slightly knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the court audience, she glimpsed him from behind a screen and was visibly displeased; the emperor sensed her dissatisfaction.

sentences.zh: 景定二年四月，帝以楊太后擁立功，乃選太后侄孫鎮尚主。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Jingding, because Empress Dowager Yang had the merit of enthroning him, the Emperor chose the Empress Dowager's grandnephew Zhen to marry the Princess.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1261, because Empress Dowager Yang had helped place him on the throne, the emperor chose her grandnephew Zhen as the princess's consort.

sentences.zh: 擢鎮右領軍衛將軍、駙馬都統，進封公主為周國公主。

translations.literal: Zhen was promoted to General of the Right Army Guard and Commander-in-Chief Attached to the Palace; the Princess was advanced to Princess of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was made a general of the Right Army Guard and commander of the imperial son-in-law's guard; the princess was promoted to Princess of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 帝俗俚時見之，乃為主起第嘉會門，飛樓閣道，密邇宮苑，帝常御小輦從宮人過公主第。

translations.literal: The Emperor, when idle, often visited her; he therefore built a residence for the Princess at Jiahui Gate, with elevated corridors and bridges close to the palace park; the Emperor often rode a small palanquin with palace women to pass by the Princess's residence.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure the emperor often visited her, so he built her a mansion at Jiahui Gate with elevated walkways near the imperial gardens; he would often ride a small carriage with palace women to her residence.

sentences.zh: 特賜董役官減三年磨勘，工匠犒賞有差。

translations.literal: He specially granted the overseers of construction a reduction of three years in their merit review, and craftsmen rewards in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He granted the construction supervisors a three-year reduction in their merit review and gave the craftsmen graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 明年，進封周、漢國公主，拜鎮慶遠軍承宣使。

translations.literal: The next year, she was advanced to Princess of Zhou and Han; Zhen was appointed Military Commissioner of Qingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she was promoted to Princess of Zhou and Han, and Zhen was made military commissioner of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 鎮宗族娣姒皆推官加封，寵異甚渥。

translations.literal: Zhen's clan, sisters-in-law, and all were advanced in office and enfeoffed—the favor shown was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Members of Zhen's clan and his wife's sisters were all promoted and ennobled—the favor shown them was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 七月，主病。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Princess fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month she fell ill.

sentences.zh: 有鳥九首大如箕，集主家擣衣石上，是夕薨，年二十二。

translations.literal: A bird with nine heads, large as a winnowing basket, alighted on the stone where clothes were beaten at the Princess's home; that night she died, aged twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: A nine-headed bird the size of a winnowing tray alighted on the laundry stone at her residence; she died that night at the age of twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 無子，帝哭之甚哀，諡端孝。

translations.literal: She had no sons; the Emperor wept for her with great grief and gave the posthumous name Duanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: She left no children; the emperor mourned her bitterly and gave her the posthumous epithet Duanxiao.

sentences.zh: 鎮官節度使云。

translations.literal: Zhen was made Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was appointed military commissioner.
